facts.text: Snellville was founded in the 1870s by Thomas Snell and James Sawyer, who secretly left England to start a trading post in the area.
The town’s name honors Thomas Snell, whose family helped preserve 130 historic letters that were returned from England in 2012.
James Sawyer, a co‑founder, died in 1948 at age 91 and is buried in the Snellville Historical Cemetery, a site the town’s society protects.
Snellville’s historic society, the only archival collection in the city, keeps records of the town’s evolution from Creek Indian land to a bustling suburb.
In the late 1990s, abandoned big‑box stores became a major issue, prompting city leaders to focus on revitalizing downtown during the 1999 elections.
Snellville sits about 25 miles northeast of Atlanta, yet its tree‑shaded streets help keep summer temperatures lower than many nearby suburbs.
